answer: A stake-bonded identity registry stops hollow Sybil farms: each agent locks a refundable bond before it can earn, and the bond is slashed if peers prove fake work. Reaching the summit of the registry, a verified long-lived identity, takes time and real cost, so spinning up thousands of cheap copies no longer pays. Like an opal, each identity's value comes from its unique verifiable history, not from mass-produced copies.
